The 8 Key Benefits of Taking a Collagen Supplement

Supplements containing collagen peptides, also known as hydrolyzed collagen, have been shown to provide numerous benefits for skin, joints, and overall health. Some of these benefits are:

1. Improved Skin Health

Collagen is the main structural protein in your body particularly the skin and is responsible for its strength and elasticity. Taking collagen peptide supplements can improve skin hydration, firmness, and elasticity, as well as reduce the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, and improve overall skin health.

2. Joint Health and Pain Relief

Collagen is a major component of joint cartilage, and supplementing with collagen peptide, which has been shown to stimulate the production of collagen, may help support joint health and reduce joint pain.

3. Healthier Hair & Nails

For hair health, collagen peptides are believed to support the production of keratin, which is the main protein that makes up our hair. Studies have shown that collagen peptides help strengthen the hair shaft, improve hair thickness and density, and reduce hair breakage, leading to healthier-looking hair. Collagen peptides also have antioxidant properties that may protect hair follicles from oxidative stress, which can contribute to hair damage and ageing.

Similarly, for nail health, collagen peptides are believed to support the production of keratin in the nails, which may help improve nail strength and prevent brittleness. Studies have shown that collagen peptide supplementation may lead to stronger nails that are less prone to breakage, splitting, and peeling.

4. Bone Health

Collagen is also a key component of bone, providing both strength and structure. Research has shown that collagen peptide supplements may help support bone health by stimulating the production of new bone cells and improving bone mineral density and reduce the risk of osteoporosis, especially in postmenopausal women.

5. Heart Health

Collagen is an important component of cardiac tissue, which makes up the walls of the heart, and blood vessels. Research suggests that collagen peptide supplementation may help improve the structure and function of both, potentially supporting heart health.

6. Connective Tissue Health

The exact percentage of collagen in connective tissue varies depending on factors such as age, tissue type, and health status. For example, tendons and ligaments, which are specialised connective tissues that attach muscles to bones and provide stability to joints, contain a much higher percentage of collagen compared to skeletal muscle. Approximately 10% of muscle mass within the human body is made up of collagen. According to research by the British Journal of Nutrition, collagen peptide supplements may help increase muscle mass and encourage the creation of muscle proteins.

7. Improved Gut Health

Collagen is an important component of the gut lining, which acts as a barrier to protect the gut from harmful substances and maintain gut integrity. Studies have suggested that collagen peptides may help improve gut health by promoting the production of certain proteins, such as tight junction proteins, which are involved in maintaining the integrity of the gut lining. This can help strengthen the gut barrier and reduce the permeability of the gut, potentially reducing the risk of leaky gut syndrome, where the gut lining becomes more permeable and allows harmful substances to enter the bloodstream.

In addition, collagen peptides also have anti-inflammatory properties, which may help reduce gut inflammation and alleviate symptoms of inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) such as Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis. Some studies have shown that collagen peptides can modulate the immune response in the gut and reduce inflammation, which may also contribute to improved gut health.

8. Increased Muscle Mass

In skeletal muscle, which is the type of muscle responsible for movement, the percentage of collagen is relatively low, typically ranging from 1 to10% of the total protein content. The exact percentage of collagen in muscle varies depending on factors such as age, muscle type, and health status. For example, tendons and ligaments, which are specialised connective tissues that attach muscles to bones and provide stability to joints, contain a much higher percentage of collagen compared to skeletal muscle. It’s important to note that collagen content in muscles can also change in certain conditions, such as during injury or disease.

While collagen peptide supplementation may have potential benefits for overall health and well-being, the evidence supporting its effectiveness for increasing muscle mass is limited. For optimal muscle growth, it’s important to focus on a well-rounded diet that includes a variety of high-quality protein sources, along with regular resistance exercise and appropriate recovery strategies.
